To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the anomalous signal from Cu Kα data can be used to solve the structure of EAS using S-SAD (native), Se-SAD (Se-Met derivative) and S/Se SIRAS (both native and Se-Met derivative) data sets, and that these methods can be used for the structure determination of any crystal with a heavy-metal content of 16 methionine residues and three cysteine residues.
the structure of Eschericia coli argininoscinate synthetase can be determined to 2.5 A resolution using Cu Kα anomalous scattering from a native protein and a Se-Met derivative.

(1) the S/Se-SAD method is a viable method of structure determination at a synchrotrons, (2) the S-Met and Se-Met derivatives of EAS can be determined at 2.0 Å resolution, (3) the S-SAD method can be used to determine a structure to 1.8 Å, and (4) the Se-SAD method can determine a structure to a similar resolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of anomalous scattering to solve structures.
the development of methods and software for the determination of the structure of proteins and nucleic acids by X-ray crystallography.

the structure of E. coli argininosuc­ cinate synthetase, an enzyme involved in the urea cycle, which catalyzes the formation of L-argininosuccinate from L-­citrulline and L-aspartate in a pyrophosphate-dependent reaction (Scheme 1).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cu Kα SAD and SIRAS are viable methods for solving protein structures, but they should be considered as a last resort when no other method can be employed.
the S-SAD method is a viable alternative to Se-SAD and Se-SIRAS methods for the determination of protein structures using Cu Kα X-ray data.
the use of Cu Kα is a viable and useful method for solving the phase problem in the case where the heavy-atom derivative is weak and/or the anomalous signal is small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S-SAD and S-SIRAS are now viable alternatives to MAD/SIRAS for the structure determination of proteins with methionines and/or cysteines.

S-SAD is the method of choice for determining structures with 16 or fewer methionines, Se-SAD is the best method for structures with 17 or more methionines, and S/Se-MAD is the best for structures with a mix of both.
the S-SAD, the Se-SAD and the S/Se-SAD methods using Cu Kα are viable alternatives to the more traditional methods of structure determination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the S/Se-SAD method can be applied to a wide range of proteins and that it can be performed with Cu Kβ radiation.
Cu Kα data are sufficient for structure solution by anomalous methods, and can be collected on a home-source rotating-anode X-ray generator.
the use of anomalous data from Cu Kα can yield high-quality structures in the 2.0–2.5 A resolution range, which is the most common range for protein structures determined at synchrotron facilities.
